title: Hydrogen storage using physisorption - materials demands
material_description: Synthetic graphite | synthetic graphite (sample No. 1); the Experimental section lists graphites among the non-porous materials
source_location: main-2.png (p. 620), Table 1, row No. 1 (Synthetic graphite), column 'H2 total'
notes: Material class coded other (graphite). Source and preparation of the synthetic graphite not stated, so synthesis_method = unknown. H2 total printed as 0 ml (STP)/g (integer rounding); stored as an exact 0 as printed. Table 1 'H2 total' at 77 K and 1 bar, printed in ml (STP)/g; uptake_wt_pct is W1 = 0.0089938 x ml(STP)/g, unrounded. 'H2 total' is the sum of the mesopore and micropore contributions (columns H2 meso + H2 micro), not a named uptake basis, so uptake_type = unspecified and basis_stated = false. H2 measured with a Micromeritics ASAP 2010 at 77 K in the pressure range 0-1 bar; measurement_method volumetric_sieverts is inferred from the instrument (a static volumetric adsorption analyser), the paper does not use the word volumetric; basis_inferred excess is the volumetric default. Only the 1-bar value of each run is reported, so no isotherm_id. 'From adsorption-desorption experiments it is evident that reversible physisorption exclusively takes place with all samples'; value taken as adsorption branch. N2 physisorption at 77 K with a Micromeritics ASAP 2400 (BET, PV, MPV, St); BET P/P0 range not stated. St (t-plot; 'the mesoporous (> 2 nm) surface area of the sorbent, i.e. the amount of surface area excluding the micropores') stored in external_surface_area_m2_g. MPV = 'pore volume of the pores < 2 nm', method not stated; PV = total pore volume. No degassing conditions, sample mass, H2 purity or free-volume calibration stated. Same value plotted in Fig. 1 (uptake vs BET area, not an isotherm). Not extracted: H2 meso = 0 and H2 micro = 0 ml (STP)/g in the same Table 1 row, computed by the authors from the t-surface correlation fitted across samples (Fig. 2); see log.md.
